analysis: Examined the three base_text units of MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (lines 526-1716) and the patch excerpt, which is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false). The change computes the reasoningPrefix from the rendered media prompt earlier, before bridge.submitTokenized (head ~714-724). It then passes a new stopStringScope (ReasoningStopScope.scope(reasoningParser:reasoningPrefix:)) into submitTokenized (head ~747-749), and the reasoningPrefix computation after submit is removed (base 750-761). Behavior change is limited to media stop-string scoping relative to the reasoning/think state. I saw no change to cache scope (cacheScope/cacheEnabled are unchanged), the donation gate, the encrypted SSD tier, or the SEC-035 TTL (T-041). I also saw no change to the E2E crypto paths, attestation, or the auth boundaries (TB-002/TB-011), and no changed memory reservation or release ordering. Reservation release is idempotent, and the catch arms still release mediaGate and releaseBox. A failure in the new prefix computation, which does not throw, would still be inside the existing do/catch. The prefix probe decodes only the rendered prompt tail, which is already in process memory, so there is no new data exposure. Residual questions beyond the supplied evidence: the head side of the diff is not fully visible. The implementation of ReasoningStopScope and the bridge's handling of stopStringScope are outside the supplied evidence. They affect only output-truncation and parsing correctness, not a confidentiality boundary. T-056 notes that correct computation is not guaranteed. No concrete regression found.
